hints: Focus on the reaction type, an alcohol with concentrated H2SO4 suggests esterification, so ask what functional group Z must contain.
Z has formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ and must be a carboxylic acid, so the ester product with propan-1-ol must contain $4 + 3 = 7$ carbon atoms in total.
Count carbons on each side of the $\text{-COO-}$ group to find which ester has a 3-carbon alcohol part from propan-1-ol and a 4-carbon acid part from Z.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

Great start. An alcohol plus another compound with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is the classic esterification condition.

$$\text{carboxylic acid} + \text{alcohol} \rightleftharpoons \text{ester} + \text{water}$$
So Z, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$, must be acting as a carboxylic acid.

**Predict the size of the ester product**

Z provides 4 carbons as the acid part. Propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, provides 3 carbons as the alcohol part.

The ester $\text{RCOO R'}$ must therefore have $4 + 3 = 7$ carbons in total, with $\text{R'}$ fixed as propyl, $\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

**Count carbons in S, T and U**

Look at each skeletal formula around the central $\text{-COO-}$:

S = propyl propanoate: 3 (alcohol) + 3 (acid) = 6 carbons. Too small.

T = propyl butanoate: 3 (alcohol) + 4 (acid) = 7 carbons. Perfect match for $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ + $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.

U = butyl propanoate: 4 (alcohol) + 3 (acid) = 7 carbons, but the alcohol part is butyl, not propyl, so it cannot come from propan-1-ol.

**Conclude the only possible product**

Only T has the correct propyl group from propan-1-ol and the correct $\text{C}_4$ acid group from Z. The branched $\text{C}_4$ acid would give a branched ester which is not shown.

options.A: Incorrect. S is propyl propanoate with only 6 carbons total. It would need a $\text{C}_3$ acid, but Z is a $\text{C}_4$ acid, so S cannot form.
options.B: Incorrect. U is butyl propanoate. Although it has 7 carbons, its alcohol part is butyl ($\text{C}_4$), which would require butan-1-ol, not the propan-1-ol used here.
options.C: Incorrect. Neither S nor U can form. S is too small ($\text{C}_6$) and U has the wrong alcohol fragment (butyl instead of propyl).
options.D: Correct. T is propyl butanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It contains the 3-carbon propyl group from propan-1-ol and the 4-carbon straight chain acid group from butanoic acid ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$).
